verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note proves a same-class three-component minimax lower benchmark and a computable conditionally honest interval, but it never bounds the interval's feasible envelope \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\) by the analytic lower envelope \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\). Consequently, the displayed lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases are proved only as lower obstructions and tuning geometry, while the estimator's risk and expected length may remain much larger or even practically trivial. The graph-only certificate pays \(BI_0(A)/n\), whereas the corresponding testing argument yields only the smaller \(B\sqrt{I_0(A)}/n\) scale, leaving another substantive mismatch. The framing prose discloses these limitations, but the title's “honest length frontier” is not delivered: what is established is a conservative finite-sample procedure plus a nonmatching lower benchmark for a distinct target on the note's maintained class.

DIRECTED IMPROVEMENT (re-derive the SAME object implementing this, do not reproduce the prior note): Strengthen the empirical-projector and bounded-difference analysis to establish sharp uniform rates for \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}\), then show that the operationally selected interval attains the supported envelope. The argument must also control the isolate contribution at the lower-benchmark scale rather than paying the current linear isolate count.
